name: follow-through
description: Stop coding agents losing unfinished work: a task tree on disk that survives pivots and context compaction, with evidence-gated closing and opt-in hooks that bring open work back into view. By Lex from SigmaStudioz.

interface.longDescription: Agents lose unfinished work when the conversation pivots, branches or is compacted. Follow-Through keeps every task on a tree saved on disk: each task has a done-when check, closes only with evidence, and a parent cannot close while a child is open. A pivot parks the current task with its next step instead of replacing it. Optional Claude Code hooks restore the open tree after a resume or compaction, remind on every prompt, and send the agent back once if it tries to stop with a task still in progress. It guarantees visibility, not completion: the user stays the judge. Standard-library Python, local files only.
defaultPrompt: Put this plan on the task tree before you start.
Park this and switch to the bug I just found.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: disk task tree with evidence-gated closing, parked pivots, session-scoped stop check and fail-open Claude Code hooks.
